[.claude/commands/eap-appr-pr.md#workflow--create-pr]

## Workflow — Create PR

1. Run `git status` to check for uncommitted changes — commit first if needed
2. Run `git log --oneline main..HEAD` to see ALL commits in the branch
3. Run `git diff main...HEAD --stat` for file-level change summary
4. Run `git diff main...HEAD` to read the FULL diff — you need this to write a detailed description
5. Ensure the branch is pushed to the remote (push with `-u` if needed)
6. **Auto-detect ADO work item from branch name:**
   - Parse the current branch name for the pattern `AB#<number>` (e.g., `feature/AB#12345-eligibility-verification`)
   - If found, pre-populate the `AB#<number>` in the Related section of the PR description and inform the user: "Detected AB#12345 from branch name — linking to ADO."
   - If no `AB#` pattern is found in the branch name, ask the user: "ADO User Story number to link? (Enter number only, or press Enter to skip)"
     - Default (empty input): proceed without ADO linking
     - If the user provides a number:
       - Validate the work item exists by querying ADO (use MCP if available, or prompt for org name and validate manually)
       - If found, append `AB#<number>` to the Related section of the PR description
       - If not found, warn the user and ask if they want to proceed anyway or enter a different number
7. Draft the PR description following the format below — be thorough and specific
8. Create the PR with `gh pr create`
9. Return the PR URL

## PR Body Format

The PR description must be detailed enough that a reviewer understands the full scope without reading every file. Do NOT use vague summaries — be specific about what changed and why.

```markdown
## Summary

<2-4 sentence overview of what this PR accomplishes and why. Include the motivation or problem being solved.>

## What Changed

### <Category or area 1> (e.g., "CI/CD Pipelines", "Skills", "Setup Scripts")
- <Specific change with file path> — <why it was changed>
- <Specific change with file path> — <why it was changed>

### <Category or area 2>
- <Specific change with file path> — <why it was changed>

(Repeat for each logical group of changes. Group by purpose, not by file type.)

## Design Decisions

- <Any non-obvious choices made and the reasoning behind them>
- <Trade-offs considered>
- <Standards or patterns followed (reference eap-ref-architecture if applicable)>

## Requirements Addressed

(If this PR implements documented requirements, list them)

| Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- |
| REQ-FN-NNN | Implemented / Partially addressed |

## Breaking Changes

<List any breaking changes, or "None" if there aren't any.>

## Test Plan

- [ ] <Specific verification step with expected outcome>
- [ ] <Specific verification step with expected outcome>
- [ ] <Regression check if applicable>

## Related

- <Link to ADO work items: AB#1234>
- <Link to related PRs, issues, or ADRs>
- <Link to relevant docs or decisions>
```

## Workflow — View / Manage PRs

- **List open PRs**: `gh pr list`
- **View a PR**: `gh pr view <number>`
- **Check PR status**: `gh pr checks <number>`
- **Review comments**: `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/<number>/comments`

[.claude/commands/eap-appr-pr.md#guidelines]

## Guidelines

- Keep PR titles under 70 characters — use the description for details
- Target `main` branch by default unless the user specifies otherwise
- **Read the full diff before writing the description** — don't guess what changed
- Group changes by purpose (not alphabetically or by file type)
- Call out non-obvious decisions, trade-offs, and standards followed
- Include specific file paths so reviewers know where to look
- If there are uncommitted changes, ask whether to commit first
- Reference ADO work items with `AB#<id>` syntax for auto-linking
